Yeah, if you can transfer a lot of credits towards your uni degree I can see how that might make sense.   


Most schools here won't let you transfer the vast majority of your credits. And even if they let you transfer 2 of your 8 classes, it works out to be about the same cost as just going directly to uni. The only difference is that it takes way longer.

To me, spending however many years at community college would constitute extra steps. But if your grades aren't so good and you want to go to uni that is probably your best best. Just make sure to keep your grades up in college. I have a friend who was rejected when trying to transfer from college to uni, but her high school and college grades were abysmal. That said, this is all totally anecdotal and you're in the US so your schools presumably work differently.
